depiction

/dih-PIK-shun/ — stress on PIK · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A depiction is a picture, description, or other representation of someone or something.

The textbook's depiction of a medieval castle labels every tower, gate, and drawbridge.

Example

The stage designer's depiction of a Paris street corner was so convincing that audience members felt they were peering through a window into another city.

de- + pict (Latin pingere, 'to paint,' also in picture and pigment) + -ion (act of) = the act of 'painting' or representing a Paris street through painted backdrops, props, and light. Depiction is the portrayal itself—how the designer chose to show that street corner for the audience. The root 'paint' reminds us that a depiction creates a picture, whether literal or in the viewer's mind.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

portrayal: A portrayal is the way someone or something is shown — the angle, tone, and choices the creator makes, fair or slanted. A depiction is the representation itself: the picture, scene, or description that results. You judge a portrayal for its fairness, a depiction for its fullness and vividness.

representation: A representation is anything made to stand for another thing — a symbol, a chart, a stick figure can all represent something. A depiction goes further than standing in: it shows its subject vividly, painting a full picture in images or words.

illustration: An illustration is a drawing made to explain or decorate something, usually sitting beside a text. A depiction can live in any medium — film, paint, prose, a mural — and the word points at how vividly the subject is shown, not at a drawing on a page.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

omission: leaving something out entirely

concealment: deliberately hiding something from view

Where it sits · how fully the subject is shown

mention → outline → sketch → depiction

mention vs. depiction: A mention names the storm in a single line, but a full depiction makes readers feel the wind and the rain.

outline vs. depiction: An outline gives just the bare shape of the battle, while the museum's depiction shows every soldier, horse, and banner.

sketch vs. depiction: A quick sketch hints at the harbor's shape; the finished painting is a rich depiction of boats, gulls, and morning light.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — depict: to paint or portray — from Latin depingere (de- + pingere, 'to paint'), past participle depictus (Latin)

Suffix — -ion: the act or process of — turns a verb into a noun (Latin (-io, -ionem))

Put it together: depict (from Latin depingere, built on pingere, 'to paint' — the same root hiding inside picture and pigment) + -ion = the act or process of picturing or representing something in images or words.

Use the root in a new word: depict: The mural on the library wall depicts the town's founding, right down to the first wooden bridge.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Reach for depiction when describing a vivid representation, portrayal, or showing of something in images, description, or narrative. It carries the sense of 'painting' a picture for an audience. Use it when the way something is represented or shown matters—in film, art, literature, or any medium where imagery or vividness is key.
